name: Ottoburg Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The historic Ottoburg at the entrance to Innsbruck's Old Town: A 15th-century Late Gothic fortified tower featuring oriel windows and fine dining.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fortified Ottoburg stands prominently at Herzog-Friedrich-Straße 1 at the gateway to the historic Old Town of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck (Innsbruck region) at an altitude of approximately 574 meters. Perched directly on the banks of the Inn River beside the Innbrücke bridge, this Late Gothic residential tower constitutes an iconic landmark of Innsbruck's historic cityscape. The mighty stone structure once served as a cornerstone of the medieval city fortifications. Local lore attributed the building to Duke Otto II of Andechs, regarded as the founder of Innsbruck in 1239, though the polygonal masonry structure seen today originates in the late 15th century under Archduke Sigismund the Rich and Emperor Maximilian I.

Architecture, Facade & Maximilian's Legacy

Architecturally, the Ottoburg impresses as a massive, five-story defensive tower with an irregular polygonal footprint. Its most striking exterior features are the distinctive red-white-red window shutters and the ornate polygonal oriel turrets resting on profiled corbels, bestowing stately elegance upon the Gothic fortification. Emperor Maximilian I acquired the property in 1497, having it sumptuously appointed for members of his imperial court. Inside, precious Late Gothic groin vaults, carved timber beam ceilings, and historic wall niches have been lovingly preserved. In front of the Ottoburg near the bridge, the famed Father and Son Monument commemorates the Tyrolean rebellion of 1809. Today, the Ottoburg houses one of Tyrol's most celebrated and traditional gourmet restaurants, offering sophisticated Alpine hospitality across historic wood-paneled parlors such as the Maximilian Room or the Dürer Room.

Visit & Getting There

As a historic architectural monument, the Ottoburg can be viewed and photographed from outside free of charge at any time. The historic dining rooms of the Restaurant Ottoburg are open year-round Tuesday to Saturday from 11:30 to 14:30 and 17:30 to 23:00 (closed on Sundays and Mondays). Dining here affords the rare privilege of savoring refined Tyrolean culinary classics and fine Austrian wines in a protected historical ambiance. Getting there: The Ottoburg marks the entrance to the Old Town pedestrian precinct at the corner of Herzog-Friedrich-Straße and Innrain. From the Golden Roof (Goldenes Dachl), it is just a two-minute walk toward the river. The IVB stop Marktplatz (lines 1, 2, A, C, J) is two minutes away on foot. Drivers can park at the adjacent Marktplatzgarage or Altstadtgarage.

Tips

The exterior view of the Ottoburg framing the rushing turquoise Inn and the pastel-colored housefronts of Mariahilf against the mountains is one of the most photographed vistas in Innsbruck. Visit around dusk when ambient street lanterns illuminate the medieval facade in romantic warm light. A visit pairs perfectly with a stroll along the sunny Inn Promenade or across the vibrant market square.
